experiments.verification_evidence: PDF page 6 image reads: 'Air-Know (Ours) | 51.03 | 73.08 | 56.76 | 75.05 | 59.47 | 79.02 | 55.75 | 75.72 | 65.73' in the 0% block. HTML cell dump row index 7 of the table: '[Air-Know (Ours)] [51.03] [73.08] [56.76] [75.05] [59.47] [79.02] [55.75] [75.72] [65.73]' under a '0%|^6' rowspan cell. assets/results-fiq.png 0% row (highlighted, sixth row of the block) reads the same nine values. The registry (workbench/registry/models.yaml:107-109) records 55.75/75.72/65.74: r10 and r50 match the paper exactly; mean is 65.74 where the paper prints 65.73 (and (55.75+75.72)/2 = 65.735). P2 registry defect, not a paper defect. GALLERY CAVEAT: neither paper nor either README states the gallery construction, the reference policy, or the candidate universe. The protocol id is a workbench inference from third_party/AirKnow/datasets.py:31 (self.split = 'original-split', hardcoded, __init__ at :29 takes only path/transform/noise_ratio) and datasets.py:218-224 (elif self.split == 'original-split': for id, image_name in enumerate(images) -> every index of split.{cat}.val.json in file order), plus the reference mask at test_BLIP2.py:147-151 before argsort at :154. The paper itself establishes none of this. The val-split pair-union branch at datasets.py:206-217 is unreachable dead code. Local split files confirm the cohort size: dress 3817 unique, shirt 6346 unique, toptee 5373 unique images in data/fashionIQ_dataset/image_splits/split.{cat}.val.json.
experiments.verification_method: Five independent routes, all agreeing cell-for-cell: (1) HTML <td> parse with rowspan/colspan on https://arxiv.org/html/2604.19386v1; (2) independent python3 html.parser parse of the same HTML; (3) pdftotext -layout of the downloaded PDF; (4) pdftoppm -f 6 -l 6 -r 200 -png render of page 6 read visually as an image; (5) the author's own results image workbench/third_party/AirKnow/assets/results-fiq.png read as an image. Routes 1/2/3/4 are the paper; route 5 is an independent author artefact. v1 vs v2 HTML Table 1 compared and identical. Arithmetic re-executed: (51.03+56.76+59.47)/3 = 55.7533 -> 55.75; (73.08+75.05+79.02)/3 = 75.7167 -> 75.72; (55.75+75.72)/2 = 65.735 -> printed 65.73.
